edition.locus: Against Marcion 2.10 (devil self-made by falsehood; free will; human victory space)

source_text: Sed et si [non] ab homine in diabolum transcripseris mali elogium, ut in instinctorem delicti, uti sic quoque in creatorem dirigas culpam ut in auctorem diaboli, — qui facit, (inquit,) angelos spiritus — ergo quod factus a deo est, id est angelus, id erit eius qui fecit, quod autem factus a deo non est, id est diabolus. id est delator, superest ut ipse sese fecerit, deferendo de deo, et quidem falsum, primo. quod deus illos ex omni ligno edere uetuisset, dehinc, quasi morituri non essent, si edissent, tertio, quasi deus illis inuidisset diuinitatem. unde igitur malitia mendacii et fallaciae in homines et infamiae in deum? a deo utique non, qui et (hunc) angelum ex forma operum bonorum instituit bonum. denique sapientissimus omnium editur ante quam diabolus; nisi malum est sapientia. et si euoluas Ezechielis prophetiam, facile animaduertes tam institutione bonum angelum illum quam sponte corruptum. in persona enim principis Sor ad diabolum pronuntiatur: et factus est sermo domini ad me dicens: fili hominis. sume planctum super principem Sor et dices: haec. dicit dominus: tu es resignaculum similitudinis, qui scilicet integritatem imaginis et similitudinis resignueris, corona decoris — hoc ut eminentissimo angelorum, ut archangelo, ut sapientissimo omnium —: in deliciis paradisi dei tui natus es; — illic enim. ubi deus in secunda animalium figurae formatione angelos fecerat. lapidem optimum indutus es. sardium, topazium. smaragdum, carbunculum, sapphirum. iaspin, lyncurium, achaten, am ethystum, chrysolithum, beryllum. onychinum, et auro replesti horrea tua et thesauros tuos. exqua die conditus es, cum Cherub imposui te in monte sancto dei, fuisti in medio lapidum igneorum. fuisti inuituperabilis in diebus tuis, ex qua die conditus es, donec inuentae sunt laesurae tuae: de multitudine negotiationis tuae promas tuas replesti et deliquisti, et cetera, quae ad suggillationem angeli, non ad illius principis proprie pertinere manifestum est eo, quod nemo hominum in paradiso dei natus sit, ne ipse quidem Adam, translatus potius illuc, nec cum Cherub impositus in monte sancto dei, id est in sublimitate caelesti, de qua satanan dominus quoque decidisse testatur, nec inter lapides igneos demoratus, inter gemmantes siderum ardentium radios, unde etiam quasi fulgur deiectus est satanas. sed ipse auctor delicti in persona peccatoris uiri denotabatur, retro quidem inuituperabilis a die conditionis suae, a deo in bonum conditus ut a bono conditore inuituperabilium conditionum et excultus omni gloria angelica et apud deum constitutus, qua bonus apud bonum, postea uero a semetipso translatus in malum. ex quo enim, inquit, apparuerunt laesurae tuae, illi eas reputans, quibus scilicet laesit hominem electum a dei obsequio. et deliquit ex illo, ex quo delictum seminauit, atque ita exinde negotiationis, id est malitiae suae, multitudinem exercuit, delictorum scilicet censum, non minus et ipse liberi arbitrii institutus, ut spiritus. nihil enim deus proximum sibi non libertate eiusmodi ordinasset. quem tamen et praedamnando testatus est ab institutionis forma libidine propria conceptae ultro malitiae , exprbitasse, et commeatum operationibus eius admetiendo rationem bonitatis suae egit, eodem consilio differens extinctionem diaboli quo hominis restitutionem. certamini enim dedit spatium.I ut et homo eadem arbitrii libertate elideret inimicum, qua succiderat illi, probans suam. non dei culpam, et ita salutem digne per uictoriam recuperaret. et diabolus amarius puniretur ab eo, quem eliserat ante, deuictus, et deus tanto magis bonus inueniretur, sustinens hominem gloriosiorem in paradisum ad licentiam decerpendae arboris uitae iam de uita regressurum.
pass_a_gloss: Angelus a Deo bonus; diabolus sese fecit. Liberum arbitrium; spatium certamini ut homo uincat.
pass_b_english: But even if you transfer the charge of evil from human to devil as instigator of the delict, so that you still direct the blame at the Creator as author of the devil—‘who makes,’ he says, ‘his angels spirits’—then what was made by God, that is the angel, will belong to him who made it; but what was not made by God, that is the devil, that is the accuser, remains for him to have made himself by accusing God—and falsely at that: first, that God had forbidden them to eat from every tree; next, as if they would not die if they ate; third, as if God had begrudged them divinity. Whence, then, the malice of lying and deceit toward humans and of infamy toward God? Certainly not from God, who also instituted this angel good after the form of good works. Finally he is published wisest of all before he is devil—unless wisdom is evil.

And if you unroll Ezekiel’s prophecy, you will easily notice that angel as good by institution and as corrupted by his own will. For in the person of the prince of Tyre it is pronounced to the devil: And the word of the Lord came to me saying: Son of man, take up a lament over the prince of Tyre and you will say: Thus says the Lord: You are the seal of likeness—who of course unsealed the integrity of image and likeness—a crown of beauty (this as most eminent of angels, as archangel, as wisest of all): you were born in the delights of your God’s paradise—for there, where God in a second formation of living figures had made angels. You were clothed with every precious stone… From the day you were created, when I set you with a cherub on God’s holy mountain, you were in the midst of fiery stones. You were blameless in your days from the day you were created until your wounds were found… It is plain these things belong to the branding of an angel, not properly to that prince, because no human was born in God’s paradise—not even Adam, who was rather transferred there—nor set with a cherub on God’s holy mountain, that is in heavenly height, from which the Lord also testifies Satan fell, nor lingering among fiery stones among the gem-like rays of burning stars, whence Satan too was cast down as lightning.

But the very author of the delict was marked in the person of a sinful man: formerly indeed blameless from the day of his condition, made by God into good as by a good maker of blameless conditions, and adorned with every angelic glory and established with God—as good with the Good—but afterward transferred by himself into evil. For from when, he says, your wounds appeared, counting those to him by which of course he wounded the human chosen away from God’s obedience. And he sinned from then, from when he sowed the delict, and so thereafter practiced a multitude of negotiation—that is of his malice—namely a census of delicts—himself no less instituted with free choice, as a spirit. For God would have ordered nothing next to himself without liberty of that kind.

Yet by also pre-condemning him he testified that he had of his own lust conceived malice beyond the form of his institution, and by measuring out leave for his operations he worked the reason of his own goodness—with the same counsel delaying the devil’s extinction by which he delayed human restoration. For he gave space for a contest, so that a human might also crush the enemy by the same liberty of choice by which he had fallen to him, proving his own—not God’s—fault, and so worthily recover salvation through victory; and that the devil might be punished more bitterly by the one he had earlier crushed, once defeated; and that God might be found so much the more good, sustaining a more glorious human about to return already from life into paradise to the leave of plucking the tree of life.

choices.choice: blame the devil’s self-corruption and free will, not the Creator’s making of the angel
rejected: trace malice back to God as author of the devil’s substance

choices.choice: read delayed judgment as room for human victory by the same liberty
rejected: call delay malice that strands humans without recovery
